title: Where Does Your Food Go?

creative.hook: Follow one imaginary bite through the digestive system and predict what happens at each stop.
creative.learningGoal: Understand how digestive organs move food, break it down, absorb nutrients, and recover water.
creative.signatureMoment: An animated bite travels through an original digestive-system diagram while each organ lights up only after the answer reveal.

researchSources.title: Your Digestive System & How it Works — National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

outroCallToAction: Ask a grown-up to subscribe and support WonderOwl Quiz!

questions.question: Which liquid moistens food and starts breaking down starch in your mouth?
questions.explanation: Saliva moistens food and contains an enzyme that begins breaking down starch.

visual.alt: A playful close-up showing saliva moistening a bite of food in the mouth
visual.answerHint: Droplets moisten food and start breaking down starch

questions.question: Can you put these first four stops of a bite's journey in order?
questions.answer: Mouth, then esophagus, then stomach, then small intestine
questions.explanation: These connected organs form the beginning of the digestive tract's route.

questions.question: True or false: Food reaches your stomach only because gravity pulls it down.
questions.explanation: Waves of muscle called peristalsis squeeze food along the esophagus.

visual.alt: A child-friendly digestive-system diagram highlighting the esophagus

questions.question: Which digestive organ am I?
clues: I receive food from the esophagus
questions.explanation: The stomach mixes food and liquid with digestive juices before releasing them gradually.

visual.alt: A child-friendly digestive-system diagram highlighting the stomach

questions.question: Which organ makes bile, a digestive juice that helps with fats?
questions.explanation: The liver makes bile, which travels to the gallbladder for storage or to the small intestine for use.

visual.alt: A child-friendly digestive-system diagram highlighting the liver

questions.question: Which small digestive organ am I?
clues: I am a small storage sac
I squeeze bile into the small intestine
questions.explanation: The gallbladder stores bile made by the liver and releases it into the small intestine.

visual.alt: A child-friendly digestive-system diagram highlighting the gallbladder

questions.question: True or false: The pancreas sends digestive juice to the small intestine.
questions.explanation: Pancreatic juice contains enzymes that help break down carbohydrates, fats, and proteins.

visual.alt: A child-friendly digestive-system diagram highlighting the pancreas

questions.question: Where are most nutrients from digested food absorbed?
questions.explanation: The walls of the small intestine absorb most nutrients and pass many of them into the bloodstream.

visual.alt: A child-friendly digestive-system diagram highlighting the small intestine

questions.question: True or false: The large intestine absorbs water from what remains after digestion.
questions.explanation: The large intestine absorbs water and changes the remaining waste from liquid into stool.

visual.alt: A child-friendly digestive-system diagram highlighting the large intestine

questions.question: Why does your body break food into much smaller parts?
options: To keep food stored in the stomach
To remove all water before absorption
To move food without muscle contractions
questions.explanation: Digestion makes nutrients small enough to support energy, growth, and cell repair.
